Dufeng Shan owns the retained essay: Great Master Huike — no book he could not explain, no scripture he had not mastered — yet before the First Founder he could not frame one word, and only then sought mind-calming; from that he dropped everything, mind like a wall; snow-standing and arm-cutting still won no nod; then one sudden breakthrough — three bows, standing in place at his station, and at last the word: you have my marrow. Senses.Explanation: Bow three times, then stand in place at your station: the answer that won the marrow — raised at hall addresses, letters, record openers, and live challenges. Xutang Zhiyu, in the hall: you will not honestly walk your own field; you only want to till the official's land under a borrowed name — do you know: the Second Founder faced Bodhidharma, bowed three times, and stood in place at his station? Baiyun Shouduan, on the raised case: who will vouch for the true line? — one saw the Akshobha realm and never saw again: skin; one held nothing against his feeling: flesh; the Second Founder bowed three times and stood in place at his station: marrow — had I seen the three of them answer so, thirty sticks each; Baiyun today is due twenty-nine himself, one stick left for all of you; whoever feels the sting neither fails the old sages nor misses Baiyun — failing that, you chew your gruel in the hall but most of you swallow it down in one muddy lump. Dufeng Shan, in the essay: Great Master Huike, no book unexplained, no scripture unmastered, could not frame one word before the First Founder and only then sought mind-calming; everything dropped, mind like a wall; snow-standing and arm-cutting won no nod; then one sudden breakthrough — three bows, standing in place, you have my marrow: was that a casual feat? — while lately students take the finger for the moon, stamp their misreading on later generations, one blind man leading a crowd of blind. Yulin Tongxiu, at the New Year small-meeting: the founders' teeth and claws, to rouse fresh spirit — Wuzu Fayan raised the founder's each-state-what-you-attained: skin, flesh, bone; last, Great Master Huike came out, bowed three times, stood in place: marrow — thirty sticks each had he seen them, this Baiyun of today due twenty-nine, one stick left for you; whoever feels the sting wrongs neither the old sages nor Baiyun; failing that, the gruel gulped down whole — and he rapped his staff: assembly! the king of the teaching has a true ear of his own.

Senses.Explanation: As before marks that an action, verdict, or condition repeats or remains unchanged. Five Lamps narrates Deng Yinfeng asking Shitou Xiqian again as before at Mazu Daoyi’s direction, and elsewhere records an unnamed monk repeating Zhaozhou Congshen’s instructed reply before Xuefeng Yicun. Fenyang Shanzhao calls a proposed recognition still not it; Zhenxie Qingliao says calculation leaves one as before; Dahui Zonggao says a person remains the same old person despite a changed label. The phrase marks continuity rather than a distinct Chan technical object.

Senses.Explanation: Baichi Yuan makes the wording concrete: after saying 'draw a gourd following the model,' he traces a circle with his hand and says, 'this is the model for the gourd.' Chan records most often use the idiom to appraise copied words or conduct in public exchanges. When a student repeats the form of an earlier answer, Gulin Qingmao calls it drawing a gourd from the model and rebukes him. Another record explicitly denies that its handling of an old case is following another's heels or drawing a gourd from the model. A later address applies the phrase across famous lineage gestures: the Buddha holding up the flower, Bodhidharma facing the wall, Linji's shout, and Deshan's staff are followed by descendants who 'each draw a gourd following the model.' The Zen deviation is this ordinary craft-copying idiom used to audit repeated case answers, gestures, verses, and recorded lineages. Since masters also use it self-referentially, the phrase is not condemnation by definition.

At a New Year's Day assembly, the head monk asks Suru Honghan about a fresh command, setting aside merely avoiding old ruts. Suru answers that mountains and rivers present no obstruction and spring reaches everywhere. The monk asks whether this means one sweep of royal influence with no borders left to guard. At the memorial observance for his teacher Zhongfeng, Tianru Weize describes a staff fierce as a tiger and alive as a dragon, once overturning sea and mountain and then disappearing where neither light nor darkness can locate it. Who says it cannot be found? It is met directly here. He presents his staff and asks whether it is simply this, immediately answering with the headword. Anyone who objects may seize it and break it in two; if no one does, he will leave it for travelers lost at night to carry sun and moon as a lantern. He strikes the staff and explains the memorial's purpose: old and new listeners should renew their resolve to settle life and death. The exact pair is Tianru's own check on an easy identification of the presented object, not a reply to a recorded audience assertion. The invitation to break it is conditional; the source does not report anyone doing so.

At the memorial observance for his teacher Zhongfeng, Tianru Weize describes a staff fierce as a tiger and alive as a dragon, once overturning sea and mountain and then disappearing where neither light nor darkness can locate it. Who says it cannot be found? It is met directly here. He presents his staff and asks whether it is simply this, immediately answering with the headword. Anyone who objects may seize it and break it in two; if no one does, he will leave it for travelers lost at night to carry sun and moon as a lantern. He strikes the staff and explains the memorial's purpose: old and new listeners should renew their resolve to settle life and death. The exact pair is Tianru's own check on an easy identification of the presented object, not a reply to a recorded audience assertion. The invitation to break it is conditional; the source does not report anyone doing so.

Senses.Note: The two warnings hold a reader between opposite mistakes. Treating the text’s words as a complete explanation wrongs the Buddhas, yet speaking apart from the text is also condemned. Senses.Explanation: The phrase is repeatedly attested. Chan masters repeatedly apply the plant-clinging image as a rebuke. Ying'an Tanhua lists striking the bench, raising the whisk, blinking, raising the eyebrows, pointing east and west, and moving the lips and tongue, then says that these still do not escape clinging to grass and attaching to trees. Chijue Daochong applies it to making a livelihood on circumstances and objects and seeking clever explanations in principle and nature. Yuanwu Keqin calls people who talk of gain and loss ‘spirits clinging to grass and attaching to trees’ (說得說失得麼。若有恁麼。盡是依草附木精靈). In his case commentary, Yuanwu sets the phrase alongside feeling along a fence and wall, while Gulin Qingmao calls an interlocutor's raised fist precisely such clinging. The bearer can be called a spirit or a person, and the criticized support changes with the passage; the headword still names the same act of dependence.

Senses.Explanation: Gave a shout is the records' stock narrative formula for one performed vocal move in a public interview or teaching-seat event. Muzhou Daoming uses it after an unnamed monk shouts at him, asks what comes after three or four shouts, and strikes when no words follow. Feiyin Tongrong shouts amid a high-seat address and says that without stopping the entangling talk with a shout it would nearly have gone on without end (若不喝住，幾乎打葛藤無有了時也). Nanyue Falun Qitian performs four shouts in sequence and labels them respectively “the lion roars,” “the elephant king stretches,” “a mad dog chases a clod,” and “a shrimp cannot leap out of the dipper”; these are four stated comparisons, not four senses. Elsewhere an unnamed monk shouts and exits, Yunfu Zhi shouts before ascending the formal seat and offering incense, and Feiyin shouts before returning to the abbot's quarters. The same formula can close an address, combine with planting the staff, or precede questions to the assembly. Chan records preserve the shout as a positioned public move; the entry reports that position and any stated classification without assigning it an unstated force.

Senses.Explanation: Under a shout is the recurrent location the Chan record gives to recognition, judgment, or failure at a recorded shout; it is not simply the shout itself. Muzhou Daoming asks how guest and host are distinguished there, while Wanru Tongwei says guest and host stand clear there. In Shimen Yuncong's record, an unnamed questioner asks what an affair under a shout is; Shimen answers that he does not engage in that business and calls it outside the questioner's sphere. Yulin Tongxiu reopens the report that Baizhang greatly awakened under Mazu's shout. The phrase does not guarantee approval. Ruixiang Zilai calls acceptance under a shout a burial of the house style; Yuanwu Keqin pairs it with catching an empty echo; Zhongfeng Mingben calls clarifying the school there dull and eye-blinding. Tianyin Yuanxiu and Wuyi Yuanlai nevertheless use the same location for knowing where to return or communicating the news. The exhaustive ledger separates this lexical construction from 319 adjacent action sequences, chiefly 'shout once' followed by 'leave the seat.'
